statement: For a quaternion with real coefficients q=(a,b,c,d), the scalar component of q times its quaternion conjugate equals a squared plus b squared plus c squared plus d squared.
source: Elementary quaternion polynomial multiplication; a local SU(2) algebra control, not a Yang-Mills existence or mass-gap claim
assumptions: a, b, c and d are commuting real scalar variables
The quaternion norm-one constraint is not proved or imposed here
This exact polynomial identity says nothing about a continuum field-theoretic spectrum
